cim: AI era places judgment, decision-making among most wanted skills
cim_eredeti: AI era places judgment, decision-making among most wanted skills
szoveg_eredeti:
Uniquely human skills will push organizations toward successful deployments as technologists become managers of AI, a Resume Now report found.

Amid AI adoption efforts, executives are chasing a mix of technical and soft skills in employees, especially as many careers, such as engineering, shift toward practicing judgment on and managing AI outputs.

As organizations mature in their AI deployment and workers navigate a changing job market, judgment and decision-making have become essential to tech jobs, the report said.

Although these skills, along with active listening or decision-making, can seem like innate personality characteristics, they are learned abilities, Spencer said. CIOs who wish to build resilient teams and develop soft skills should give room for experimentation, provide criticism and feedback to learn from and expect failure at times, Spencer said.

As AI handles routine and deeper work within the enterprise, organizations need people who can interpret outputs, recognize potential errors and make informed decisions, he said. Developing a diverse skill set and staying adaptable while working with rapidly changing technology is essential, Spencer said.

“Developing AI literacy or proficiency cannot be ignored, but you also don't want to, at the same time, neglect your uniquely human skills,” Spencer said.

Workers that treat AI tools as collaborators that need direction and insight tend to perform better than those who simply delegate tasks to it, according to a study from the McCombs School of Business at the University of Texas at Austin and KPMG.

Interpersonal and soft skills are desirable in tech leadership as well as with employees. Critical thinking was a skill long desirable before AI, but the technology has brought new importance to an employee’s abilities, Spencer said.

“We encourage people to evaluate the information they’re given from multiple angles … and carefully review AI-generated recommendations, rather than just accepting them automatically,” Spencer said.
